mandatoryFindings.title: Optimized Python removes the common loader integrity barrier before adapter compilation
mandatoryFindings.evidence: All mode/path/custody/size/read-race/raw-SHA checks in the common loader use assert. The canonical -B -c launch neither ignores PYTHONOPTIMIZE nor explicitly rejects optimized execution, and the adapter has no prior executable precondition that can restore a barrier already bypassed before its code is compiled. Four guarded actual-loader bytecode cases show valid buffers accepted in normal/optimized modes; wrong expected SHA denies under optimize=0 but reaches adapter compile and requested execution under optimize=1. The reviewer intercepted that execution; no actual adapter/main or OS operation ran. No actual host optimization setting is asserted.
mandatoryFindings.requiredCorrection: In a new exact successor make the precompile integrity/custody/argument checks non-removable explicit checks, or reject optimized execution using an explicit non-assert branch before any loader read/compilation and enforce that exact protocol on guard plus all ordinary/postclose entries. Keep the common literal identical across paths, bind its new bytes and APIs in all active metadata, and retain wrong-hash/custody/argument denial under optimized as well as ordinary compilation. Preserve all727 semantic cases and unchanged Java/source/business scope; do not mutate source04 or alter actual runtime configuration during preparation.
